database_summary: This is a Formula 1 / motorsport race results dataset (SQLite) with tables describing races, circuits, drivers, constructors, race results, lap times, pit stops, qualifying, standings, and several extended/enriched tables. Core event/fact tables (results, lap_times, pit_stops, qualifying, retirements, lap_positions, sprint_results, constructor_results) record per-race/per-driver/per-lap measurements or events. Dimension-like tables (drivers, constructors, circuits, status, seasons, short_* and *_ext tables) provide descriptive attributes. Several tables are aggregated or precomputed (driver_standings, constructor_standings, driver_standings_ext, lap_time_stats, team_driver_ranks). Many tables use consistent integer surrogate primary keys; some legacy/extended tables use composite natural keys. Be careful: several tables with foreign-key semantics do not declare FK constraints in DDL here; use column name conventions (race_id, driver_id, constructor_id, circuit_id, status_id) to join. Joins between one-to-many event tables and dimensions can multiply rows (e.g., joining results to lap_times multiplies by number of laps).

accepted.name: race_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time
FROM races
accepted.description: Normalized race rows with canonical typed date/time and key descriptive columns. Use this as the canonical race dimension for joins and time-based filters. | Use for: List races by year/round/date; Join races to results/pit_stops/qualifying; Filter races that had a sprint or specific session

accepted.name: driver_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Canonical driver dimension preserving identifiers and name parts for joins and display. Use when queries need driver attributes or to join driver events. | Use for: Look up driver names/nationality/age; Join drivers to results, lap_times, pit_stops, standings

accepted.name: constructor_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructor_id,
  constructor_ref,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors
accepted.description: Canonical constructor/team dimension preserving identifiers and descriptive attributes for joins. | Use for: List constructor names/nationalities; Join constructors to results/standings

accepted.name: race_results_w_driver_constructor
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.constructor_id,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.position_text,
  r.position_order,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.rank,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.status_id,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  d.number AS number__driver,
  c.name AS name,
  c.constructor_ref
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON r.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON r.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
accepted.description: Denormalized results joined to driver and constructor attributes. One row per result (result_id) with driver/constructor descriptive columns and race key for easy analysis. | Use for: Show finishing positions with driver/constructor names; Compute driver/constructor points per race; Filter results by driver or constructor attributes

accepted.name: driver_lap_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS lap_count,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_milliseconds,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_milliseconds,
  MIN(lap) AS first_lap,
  MAX(lap) AS last_lap
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Per race_id + driver_id aggregated lap-time measures: lap count, min/avg/max milliseconds and best lap (min). Useful for performance summaries per stint/driver in a race. | Use for: Compare driver lap consistency in a race; Find drivers with fastest single-lap in a race; Filter for drivers who completed a minimum number of laps

accepted.name: pit_stops_per_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(*) AS pit_stop_count,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_pit_milliseconds,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_pit_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_pit_milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Aggregated pit stop metrics per race and driver: number of stops, average and minimum pit milliseconds. Use for pit strategy analysis. | Use for: Compare pit stop counts and durations per driver/race; Identify drivers with unusually long/short pit stops

accepted.name: qualifying_grid_with_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  c.name AS name,
  c.constructor_ref
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON q.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON q.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
accepted.description: Qualifying entries joined to driver and constructor details, one row per qualify_id (driver in qualifying). Useful to inspect starting grid and qualifying times (q1/q2/q3). | Use for: Show starting grid with driver names and qualifying lap times; Compare qualifying performance vs race results

accepted.name: driver_season_points
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ryear AS year,
  driver_id,
  SUM(points) AS season_points,
  COUNT(DISTINCT race_id) AS races_entered
FROM (
  SELECT rs.race_id, ra.year AS ryear, rs.driver_id, rs.points
  FROM results rs
  LEFT JOIN races ra ON rs.race_id = ra.race_id
)
GROUP BY ryear, driver_id
accepted.description: Season-to-date points per driver and year aggregated from driver_standings or results. Useful to rank drivers by season points or examine point progression. (Prefer driver_standings table for season snapshots; this aggregate uses results.points as fallback.) | Use for: Rank drivers by season points; Compare driver season totals across years; Find drivers with most race entries in a season

accepted.name: race_fastest_lap_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS best_lap_milliseconds,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY race_id ORDER BY MIN(milliseconds) ASC) AS best_lap_rank
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Per race, rank drivers by their best lap (minimum milliseconds) using lap_times. Exposes best_lap_milliseconds and best_lap_rank to support top-k fastest drivers in a race. | Use for: Find the top-N fastest lap performers per race; Compare best lap ranks to final results

accepted.name: driver_running_points_by_season
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  driver_id,
  race_id,
  race_date,
  points,
  SUM(points) OVER (PARTITION BY year, driver_id ORDER BY race_date, race_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_points
FROM (
  SELECT ra.year, rs.driver_id, rs.race_id, ra.date AS race_date, rs.points
  FROM results rs
  LEFT JOIN races ra ON rs.race_id = ra.race_id
) sub
accepted.description: Running (cumulative) points for each driver within a season ordered by race date. Useful to plot championship progression or compute lead changes. Uses races.date to order events. | Use for: Plot driver championship trajectories; Compute when a driver clinched the championship (downstream filter by cumulative points)

accepted.name: latest_driver_standing_per_season
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  ds.driver_standings_id,
  ds.race_id,
  ra.year,
  ds.driver_id,
  ds.points,
  ds.position,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ra.year, ds.driver_id ORDER BY ds.race_id DESC) AS rn
FROM driver_standings ds
LEFT JOIN races ra ON ds.race_id = ra.race_id
accepted.description: Pick the latest available driver_standings row per year and driver based on race_id ordering. Exposes position and points as the most recent snapshot for that driver in the season. | Use for: Get final season standings (filter rn = 1 per year/driver); Compare mid-season vs final standings by selecting different rn values
